Corrections.PreviousClaim: snprintf may write 1024 non-zero bytes with no NUL, and the implicit conversion to std::string reads past buffer until a zero byte.
Corrections.CorrectedClaim: The buffer IS null-terminated by snprintf within buf_size; the real defect is the unguarded return buffer; at line 222, which returns possibly-uninitialized stack bytes. The previous rationale cited the wrong source line (221, snprintf) instead of line 222, and no ground-truth item exists for this finding, so no detection credit was granted.

truthAudit.Summary: Run 2 had 12 findings. Against the 20 confirmed ground-truth vulnerabilities: 10 were found (SC-V3-001, -002, -003, -004, -005, -008, -009, -010, -020), 2 partially (SC-V3-007 emergency-bypass/lockout-bypass noted only as secondary evidence for the credential finding; SC-V3-014 persistent auth state noted only as secondary evidence), and 10 were missed (SC-V3-006, -011, -012, -013, -015, -016, -017, -018, -019). No previous-answer detection claim was overstated: every found_full/found_partial claim is backed by an exact quoted rationale, and no claim was upgraded after seeing the ground truth. All 10 previous citations to source lines were accurate. 10 corrections are required: severity undercalls on SC-V3-001/003/004 (High→Critical), SC-V3-002 (Medium→High), plus CWE corrections on SC-V3-005 (CWE-787→CWE-120/121), SC-V3-008 (CWE-699→CWE-22), SC-V3-009 (CWE-121→CWE-122), SC-V3-002 (CWE-192→CWE-190), and SC-V3-020 (CWE-542→CWE-369), plus one evidence correction: the previous format_string finding attributed non-null-termination to snprintf, but snprintf guarantees a NUL within buf_size; the actual gap is the unguarded `return buffer;` at line 222.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Line 237: 'std::string active_format = runtime_log_format();'. Line 238: 'printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input);'. The format string is set from an attacker-controlled config value via line 556 ... while line 604 passes the admin command (user input) as the argument.
Items.Notes: The audited answer quotes source lines 237-238 exactly and states that the format string originates from config::security::LOG_FORMAT, which load_config sets from an unvalidated file value, and that the user-supplied argument reaches printf via admin exec. Both conditions required by SC-V3-001 (runtime_log_format; printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input)) are present.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Line 316-318: 'for (long long i = 2; i <= static_cast<long long>(x); i++) { result *= i; }'. There is no upper bound on x. For x >= ~21 the multiplication overflows signed long long (UB).
Items.Notes: The previous answer quotes the exact loop at lines 316-318 with `result *= i` and correctly reports signed-integer overflow UB. Trigger `fact(100)` is supported by the source at lines 863-868.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Lines 813-828: stage_deferred_history_flush() allocates each scratch buffer from memory::g_memory_pool (line 817: 'char* scratch = static_cast<char*>(memory::g_memory_pool.allocate(copy_len + 1));') ... Lines 883-884: cleanup() then calls stage_deferred_history_flush() and immediately calls memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup() ... with no wait for the queued worker threads to finish.
Items.Notes: The previous answer quotes lines 813-828 and 883-884 and correctly describes pool allocation of scratch, worker enqueueing of deferred reads, and pool cleanup executed without joining the pool. Required anchors (stage_deferred_history_flush; memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup) are all cited.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Lines 564-567: 'std::string validator_cmd = get_setting("validator_path", "/usr/bin/validator"); std::string config_file = get_setting("config_file", "default.conf"); std::string command = validator_cmd + " " + config_file; int result = system(command.c_str());'. Both values come from an unvalidated config file and are concatenated into a shell command.
Items.Notes: Exact quotes of lines 564-567 and a correct description of validator_cmd + " " + config_file being passed to system(command.c_str()) from an attacker-writable config file, reachable through admin validate (line 614-615).

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Line 831: 'if (expression.length() >= sizeof(input_buffer_)) {'. Line 832: 'strcpy(input_buffer_, expression.c_str());'. ... input_buffer_ is a fixed member array of 1024 bytes (line 664, config::limits::STACK_BUFFER_SIZE). No length limit is enforced on the caller input before this function is reached (line 690).
Items.Notes: The previous answer quotes lines 831-832 and 664 and correctly states that expressions of 1024+ bytes take the strcpy branch in evaluate_expression, overflowing input_buffer_. Required anchors (strcpy(input_buffer_; src_len > dest_size pattern) and stack input processing) are all present.

The audited answer contains no finding for the thread-pool counter race. Source lines 483-485 read `value_` (volatile long long) outside the mutex and write under lock_guard; line 488's `get()` performs an unlocked read with no happens-before edge to a writer, so concurrent readers can observe stale values. Required anchors (volatile long long; old_value = value_; lock_guard; value_ = old_value + 1) are entirely absent.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: the lockout count never resets and can be defeated via the string-substring bypass
Items.Notes: The previous answer reported the EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE substring bypass and noted that login_attempts_ (never reset) gates it, which covers the logic-bomb trigger, but never elevated it as its own CWE-511 logic-bomb finding, classifying it only as secondary evidence inside the CWE-798 credential finding.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Line 543: 'std::string full_path = config_dir_ + filename;'. Line 544 only checks 'std::filesystem::exists(full_path)'. filename comes from user input ... so '..' or absolute paths are accepted
Items.Notes: Exact quotes of lines 543-544, config_dir_ + filename concatenation, and the unvalidated filename path from admin load (line 611-612). Full coverage of SC-V3-008 anchors.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Line 366: 'buffer_size_ = 256;'. ... Line 374-376: 'std::string expr_str; for (const auto& token : tokens) expr_str += token.text + " "; if (expr_str.length() > 0) strcpy(expression_buffer_, expr_str.c_str());'. The serialized token string can exceed 256 bytes and is copied with strcpy with no bounds check.
Items.Notes: Exact quotes of lines 366, 374-376 and a correct statement that an unbounded serialized token string is copied with strcpy into a 256-byte pool allocation. Required anchors (buffer_size_ = 256; strcpy(expression_buffer_; schedule_expression_analysis)) are all covered.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Line 573: 'constexpr char ADMIN_SECRET[] = "SC_ENT_2025_AUTH";'. ... Comparison is plaintext equality, the lockout count never resets and can be defeated via the string-substring bypass.
Items.Notes: Exact quote of line 573 (ADMIN_SECRET = SC_ENT_2025_AUTH) plus the plaintext equality comparison at line 587 and the EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE bypass. Full coverage of the hardcoded-credential vulnerability.

The audited answer contains no finding for the session token generator. Source lines 637-639 use std::random_device once, std::mt19937, and std::uniform_int_distribution<> dis(1000, 9999), yielding predictable 4-digit tokens of the form 'TOKEN_####'. Required anchors (std::mt19937; uniform_int_distribution; 1000, 9999) are absent.

No finding for the timestamp cache race. Source lines 230-231 declare `static std::tm cached_time;` and read it back with cached_time = *local_time while log_debug_message is callable concurrently from main's evaluation path and the thread pool, making it a shared non-atomic mutable state (CWE-362). Anchors (static std::tm cached_time; localtime; cached_time = *local_time) are absent.

No finding for temp-file handling. Source lines 624-633 in append_override_audit_event() form a command string from TMPDIR/TMPDIR-derived paths (including the attacker-supplied path embedded in an admin session) and run it with system(command.c_str()); the log file supercalc_emergency.log is therefore attacker-influenceable. Required anchors (TEMP; TMPDIR; supercalc_emergency.log; system(command.c_str())) are absent.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Comparison is plaintext equality, the lockout count never resets and can be defeated via the string-substring bypass
Items.Notes: The previous answer observed that login_attempts_ is only incremented (line 586) and never reset, and that a session token is retained after successful authentication. However, it never asserted this as a standalone CWE-613 persistent-authentication-state finding, so the detection credit for SC-V3-014 is only partial.

No finding for exception safety in variable parsing. Source line 729 calls std::stod(tokens[3]) inside handle_variable_command with no try/catch, so a non-numeric value reaches std::terminate. Related anchors (std::stod(tokens[3]); handle_variable_command) are absent.

No finding for the memory-pool split underflow. Source line 133 computes `size_t remaining = previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES;` when the guard only checks previous_size > size, so splitting a block smaller than SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES (64) underflows remaining, which then becomes fragment.size (line 136), yielding an absurdly large split fragment. Anchors (SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES; previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES; fragment.size = remaining) are absent.

No finding for parser recursion. Source lines 381-433 have parse_expression recursing through parse_term/parse_factor with no depth cap, while config::limits::MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH = 256 (line 665) is never enforced. Deeply nested parentheses such as '((((((...)))))' overflow the native stack. Anchors (parse_expression; parse_factor; PAREN_OPEN) are absent.

No finding for the result-cache race. Source line 445-451 reads `result_cache_.find(expression)` and returns `cached->second` without holding cache_mutex_, while other threads populate/clear the cache concurrently; additionally evaluate_cached takes a non-atomic std::string expression key. Anchors (result_cache_; evaluate_cached; cache_mutex_; thread_pool_->enqueue) are absent.

No finding for the config-loading TOCTOU. Source lines 543-546 call std::filesystem::exists(full_path), then std::this_thread::sleep_for(25ms) (line 545), and only afterwards open std::ifstream file(full_path); an attacker can race the file swap in the 25 ms window. Anchors (std::filesystem::exists; sleep_for; std::ifstream file) are absent.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Lines 750-752: 'size_t token_end = input.find_first_of(" \t"); size_t token_length = (token_end == std::string::npos) ? input.length() : token_end; return 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length);'. When the input begins with a space or tab, token_end is 0 and the division is by zero.
Items.Notes: Exact quotes of lines 750-752, a correct zero-length-token condition, and the trigger (expression starting with a space/tab, reached from run() line 684). Detection credit is full; only the CWE classification was wrong.
